column1: I've got all of Rocklin's belongings in an envelope over on the counter for you.
column2: 我把 Rocklin 的所有物品放在櫃檯上的信封裡，等著你來拿。

column1: I see you found that manilla envelope I put out for you.  The stuff in there was Rocklin's.
column2: 我看你找到了我給你留的那個牛皮信封。裡面的東西都是 Rocklin 的。

column1: I found this under the fingernails of your murder victim, Andrew Dent.  A little skin, a little hair...   Think of it as my gift to you.
column2: 我在你那位謀殺案被害人 Andrew Dent 的指甲下面找到了這個。一點皮膚，一些頭髮……當成是我送你的禮物吧。

column1: Hey, drop by for lunch some time!  I'll slice us up some fresh pastrami!
column2: 嘿，改天中午來吃個飯啊！我給你切點新鮮的培根肉！

column1: Hey, Bonds... you ok?  You look a little green around the gills!
column2: 嘿，Bonds……你沒事吧？你臉色有點難看啊！

column1: Nope.  Nobody you know.  There's a toe tag, though.
column2: 沒有。不是你認識的人。不過有驗屍編號標籤。

column1: You notice a toe tag.
column2: 你注意到了驗屍編號標籤。

column1: This corpse's feet look particularly unattractive.  You notice a toe tag.
column2: 這具屍體的腳看起來特別讓人不舒服。你注意到了驗屍編號標籤。

column1: The drawers store bodies.  You wonder if there's anyone you know in there.
column2: 這些抽屜裡存放的是屍體。你心想不知道裡面有沒有認識的人。

column1: I'm starting to worry about you Bonds.
column2: 「我開始擔心你了，Bonds。」

column1: Leon Mandel is the County Coroner.  It's rare to see him without something or other in his mouth.  He's a little strange, but you've come to appreciate his sense of humor.
column2: Leon Mandel 是郡驗屍官。要看到他嘴裡沒有東西的時候很罕見。他有點奇怪，但你已經學會欣賞他的幽默感了。

column1: Leon's not about to share his sandwich.
column2: Leon 不太可能分享他的三明治。

column1: Nah.  He might enjoy it.
column2: 不會。他說不定還挺享受的。

column1: Hey, you want a picture?  I'll send you an autographed one.  Me in my polka dot swim trunks.  No problem.
column2: 嘿，你想要張照片嗎？我可以寄給你一張簽了名的。我穿著圓點泳褲的照片。沒問題。

column1: Whaddaya want from me, a medal?  Your evidence boys down at the station have the time and equipment for all that lab analysis stuff.  Me, I'm busy enough with just the stiffs.
column2: 你想從我這裡要什麼，一枚勳章？你們局裡的鑑識組有時間和設備做那些實驗室分析工作。我呢，光是忙著應付這些死人就夠累的了。

column1: Better hang on to it!
column2: 最好好好保管它！

column1: There's a large manilla envelope on the counter.
column2: 櫃檯上有一個大牛皮信封。

column1: Knowing what a strange individual Leon is, you decide to stay out of his cabinets.
column2: 考慮到 Leon 有多古怪，你決定別去翻他的櫃子。

column1: Leon certainly has a lot of storage space in here.
column2: Leon 這裡確實有很多儲存空間。

column1: Even if Leon GAVE you that chart, you wouldn't take it.
column2: 即使 Leon 把那張圖表送給你，你也不會要。

column1: You'd rather not look at that chart on the wall.  You see enough of that stuff at accident scenes.
column2: 你寧願不看牆上那張圖表。你在車禍現場看過夠多那類東西了。

column1: You don't have much call for embalming fluid, Sergeant.
column2: 防腐液對你這位警佐用處不大。

column1: The bottles contain embalming fluid.
column2: 這些瓶子裡裝的是防腐液。

column1: There'll be time enough for you to be on the table when you're dead.
column2: 等你死了以後，會有充足的時間讓你上解剖台。

column1: The sight of the cold, stainless steel autopsy table sends a chill through the spine as you recall the many times you've come close to ending up on one.
column2: 看到冷冰冰的不鏽鋼解剖台，你脊背發涼，回想起自己曾經好幾次險些躺上去。

column1: This isn't "Life & Death".  There's a REASON you didn't go into forensics.  Just looking at those instruments makes you queasy.
column2: 這不是「生死時刻」。你沒有從事法醫工作是有原因的。光是看著那些工具就讓你感到噁心。

column1: A number of cruel-looking stainless steel instruments lie on a towel on the counter.
column2: 一些看起來很殘酷的不鏽鋼儀器放在櫃檯上的毛巾上。

column1: You'd better leave "Demi" alone.  You know how Leon is about his bones.
column2: 你最好別碰「Demi」。你知道 Leon 對他的骨頭有多執著。

column1: That's Leon's 'girlfriend', Demi Bones.
column2: 那是 Leon 的「女友」，Demi Bones。

column1: The toe tag reads "%s".
column2: 驗屍編號標籤上寫著「%s」。

column1: Good old Leon.  He has so much fun naming the John Does.
column2: 老天啊 Leon。他給無名屍取名的時候可開心了。

column1: The toe tag reads "%s" - the poor stiff you found in the alley.
column2: 驗屍編號標籤上寫著「%s」——你在巷子裡找到的那具可憐的屍體。

column1: Underneath the name is a note:  "Bonds - Caught you peeking!  Stepped out for a bite.  Be back soon - Leon."
column2: 名字下面有一張紙條：「Bonds——抓到你在偷看！出去吃口東西去了。待會兒回來——Leon。」

column1: This place does have a way of making you want to wash your hands, doesn't it?
column2: 這個地方確實有種讓人想洗手的感覺，是吧？

column1: The Coroner's office is equipped with a sink.  You hate to think about what washes down those drains!
column2: 驗屍官辦公室裡有一個水槽。你不想去想那些排水管裡沖下去的是什麼東西！

column1: I don't think Leon would appreciate your playing with his toys.
column2: 我不認為 Leon 會歡迎你去玩他的玩意兒。

column1: The embalming machine is a kind of mechanical vampire.  Out with the old, in with the new...
column2: 防腐機就像某種機械吸血鬼。把舊的吸出去，把新的灌進來……

column1: You ignore the firemen and walk right into the burning house. Falling debris hits you on the head, and you succumb to the flames.
column2: 你無視消防隊員走直進燃燒的房子裡。掉落的殘骸砸中了你的頭，你被火焰吞沒了。

column1: I'll deal with the gawkers across the street.
column2: 我會去應付街對面那些看熱鬧的人。

column1: Just try to conduct yourself like a professional.  OK, Morales?
column2: 試試看能不能表現得像個專業人士。好嗎，Morales？

column1: No prob' Boss man!
column2: 沒問題，老闆！

column1: Ok folks! Who brought the marshmallows, huh?
column2: 好吧各位！誰帶棉花糖來了，嗯？

column1: I'll go take care of the gawkers across the street, Sonny.
column2: 我去應付街對面那些看熱鬧的人，Sonny。

column1: What appears to have started the fire?
column2: 火看起來是怎麼起的？

column1: Looks like arson to me. She went up awful fast.
column2: 在我看來像是縱火。火勢上來得很快。

column1: Do you have any idea who might have started it?
column2: 你有沒有想過誰可能幹的？

column1: It's under investigation. You can go in if you like.
column2: 正在調查中。如果你願意可以進去。

column1: You thank the fire chief and let him get back to work.
column2: 你向消防隊長道謝，讓他回到工作崗位。

column1: Hey you!  Get back away from the fire line!
column2: 嘿你！退到火災警戒線以外去！

column1: Officer, I found something you might want to look at.
column2: 警官，我找到了東西，你可能想看看。

column1: It looks like a photograph.
column2: 看起來像是一張照片。

column1: It takes you a moment to realize what you're seeing.  You feel goosebumps crawl up your back.
column2: 你花了一陣子才意識到自己看到了什麼。你感到雞皮疙瘩爬上後背。

column1: The man on the left is none other than your one-time arch nemesis, Jessie Bains.  The man on the right bears a striking resemblance to him.
column2: 左邊的人不是別人，正是你曾經的死對頭 Jessie Bains。右邊的人長得和他有驚人的相似。

column1: You don't believe this!  The Bains brothers, Michael and Jessie.
column2: 你無法相信！Bains 兄弟，Michael 和 Jessie。

column1: The firemen are struggling to put out the fire.
column2: 消防隊員正在努力撲滅大火。

column1: The firemen are anxious to get this wrapped up.
column2: 消防隊員急著要把這場火撲滅。

column1: The fire's under control. Not to worry.
column2: 「火勢已經控制住了。不用擔心。」

column1:
Hey, we're off call as soon as we're done here. Who wants to grab a beer down at Johnny's?	「嘿，我們一完成就下班。誰想去 Johnny's 喝杯啤酒？
We've almost got it out now."
column2: 「我們差不多要把它撲滅了。」

column1: Man, I gotta call my wife. Anybody seen a phone?
column2: 「天啊，我得給我老婆打個電話。有人看到電話嗎？」

column1: This fire's nothing compared to the office building that went up yesterday.
column2: 「這場火比昨天那棟辦公樓的火小多了。」

column1: This one didn't take long at all. At least we caught it before it spread up the street.
column2: 「這場火沒花多長時間。至少我們在它蔓延到街上之前控制住了。」

column1: It looks like the man with the bull horn is in charge. He must be the fire chief.
column2: 看起來那個拿著擴音器的人是負責人。他應該是消防隊長。

column1: The fire chief is focused on his men. He doesn't notice you.
column2: 消防隊長專注於他的手下。他沒有注意到你。

column1: You see the fire gutted shell of a house still ablaze. It looks like the fire fighters have it under control.
column2: 你看到了被火燒成空殼的房子還在燃燒。看起來消防隊員已經控制住了火勢。

column1: You see the fire gutted shell of a house.
column2: 你看到了被火燒成空殼的房子。

column1: It's a Lytton Fire Department pumper.
column2: 這是 Lytton 消防局的消防車。

column1: The firemen have the fire well in hand and don't need your assistance.
column2: 消防隊員完全控制住了火勢，不需要你的協助。

column1: It's the trunk of your car.
column2: 這是你車的後備廂。

column1: It looks like a photograph.  You pick it up.
column2: 看起來像是一張照片。你撿了起來。

column1: You notice something shiny sticking out from under a mound of burnt refuse.
column2: 你注意到在一堆燒焦的垃圾底下有什麼閃閃發亮的東西露出來。

column1: The walls are marred by fire.
column2: 牆被火燒得滿目瘡痍。

column1: You don't want to touch that.  Some of this stuff is still hot.
column2: 你不想碰那個。有些東西還是熱的。

column1: The ugly old couch is soaked and smoldering.  The smell\nof burnt upholstery stings your nose.
column2: 那張醜陋的舊沙發又濕又冒著煙。燒焦家具的味道\n刺激著你的鼻子。

column1: The smoking couch does not interest you.
column2: 冒著煙的沙發引不起你的興趣。

column1: The carpet has melted in places into a molten polyester mess.
column2: 地毯有些地方融化成了熔化的聚酯塑膠。

column1: You search this area but find nothing.
column2: 你搜索了這個區域但什麼都沒找到。

column1: The cushion doesn't interest you.
column2: 這個靠墊引不起你的興趣。

column1: The melted glob doesn't interest you.
column2: 這灘融化的東西引不起你的興趣。

column1: This appears to some sort of altar room. You get the feeling you're not dealing with kids and ouija boards here.
column2: 這看起來像是某種祭壇房間。你有一種感覺，這不是什麼小孩子和通靈板的把戲。

column1: You carefully scrape off some of the dried blood and hair and put them in an envelope.
column2: 你小心地刮下一些乾掉的血液和頭髮，放進一個信封裡。

column1: You need something with which to collect a clean sample.
column2: 你需要某種東西來採集乾淨的樣本。

column1: Even the idea of touching this sicko stuff disgusts you.
column2: 連想到要碰這些變態東西都讓你感到厭惡。

column1: A pentagram has been carefully painted on the wooden floor with red paint.
column2: 一個五角星被細心地用紅漆畫在木地板上。

column1: As you study the floor within the altar you notice a dried puddle of blood and hair. It appears to be the remains of some sick sacrificial ritual. Your stomach turns.
column2: 當你研究祭壇內的地板時，你注意到一灘乾掉的血液和頭髮。看起來是某種病態祭祀儀式的遺跡。你感到反胃。

column1: You don't want to touch that. Some of this stuff is still hot.
column2: 你不想碰那個。有些東西還是熱的。

column1: The last embers of the fire cast an eerie red glow throughout the smokey house.
column2: 火最後的餘燼在煙霧瀰漫的房子裡投射出詭異的紅色光芒。

column1: The pipe doesn't interest you.
column2: 這根管子引不起你的興趣。

column1: Exposed water pipes and charred studs are all that remain of some of the interior walls.
column2: 露出的水管和燒焦的立柱是一些內牆僅存的東西。

column1: Good day, Sir! Good day! You look like a man in need of a career.
column2: 早安，先生！早安！你看起來像是需要一份職業的人。

column1: Reconsidering?
column2: 重新考慮一下？

column1: You made an excellent choice! The army's the ONLY life for a man!
column2: 你做了個絕妙的選擇！軍隊才是一個男人唯一的人生！

column1: Outdoor adventure, free room and board, good old-fashioned discipline! Get all those newfangled, namby-pamby, TV-zombie ideas out of your system and get your life back under control. Know what I mean?
column2: 戶外冒險，免費的食宿，傳統的紀律！把那些新花樣、婦人之心、被電視洗腦的想法都趕出你的腦子，把你的人生重新控制住。你明白我的意思嗎？

column1: Serving you is a pleasure, sir. Don't forget the U.S. Army if you ever need a change of careers!
column2: 為你服務是我的榮幸，先生。如果你將來想換個職業，別忘了美國軍隊！

column1: Thanks. I won't.
column2: 謝了。我不會的。

column1: You can even choose your first tour of duty.
column2: 你甚至還可以選擇你的第一個任期。

column1: Remember, son. It's the best character builder a man could want.
column2: 記住，小夥子。這是一個男人能夠得到的最好的品格塑造。

column1: At the end of your six year enlistment, you'll be amazed at how the time just flew by.
column2: 在你六年役期結束時，你會驚訝時間過得有多快。

column1: Just think of an exciting career in heavy tank repair!
column2: 想想一個令人興奮的重型坦克維修職業吧！

column1: You could become a career man. Look at what it's done for me.
column2: 你可以成為一個職業軍人。看看它對我做了什麼。

column1: We have many exciting bases around the world, like Oklahoma.
column2: 我們在世界各地有很多令人興奮的基地，比如俄克拉荷馬。

column1: Hmmm... That sounds terrific, but I already have got a good career, thanks.
column2: 嗯……聽起來很不錯，但我已經有份不錯的工作了，謝了。

column1: You show the photograph to the recruiting officer again.
column2: 你再次把照片展示給徵兵官看。

column1: You show the photograph of Jessie and Michael Bains to the recruiting officer.
column2: 你把 Jessie 和 Michael Bains 的照片展示給徵兵官看。

column1: Well, why didn't you say who you were earlier? Of course I can get that information for you, Sergeant.
column2: 那你為什麼剛才不說你是誰呢？當然，我可以為你查那些資訊，警佐。

column1: Can you give me any information on this man? His name is Michael Bains. He should have a military record.
column2: 你能告訴我關於這個人的任何資訊嗎？他叫 Michael Bains。他應該有軍事檔案。

column1: That's privileged information there, boy! The U.S. Army doesn't hand out military records to just anyone!
column2: 那是保密資訊，夥計！美國軍隊不會隨便把軍事檔案交給任何人！

column1: Let me see here, Sergeant...
column2: 讓我找找看，警佐……

column1: Ah! Here we go. Michael Bains. Let me get you a printout.
column2: 啊！找到了。Michael Bains。讓我給你列印一份。

column1: There you are, Sergeant. Hope it helps.
column2: 給你，警佐。希望有幫助。

column1: You show the recruiting officer your badge and identify yourself.
column2: 你把警章給徵兵官看，報出你的身份。

column1: He looks closely at your credentials, making sure they're legitimate. When he looks up, he seems more cooperative.
column2: 他仔細查看你的證件，確保它們是真實的。當他抬起頭時，他似乎更願意配合了。

column1: Yes, Sir, Sergeant. And what can I do for you today?
column2: 是的，警佐。我今天可以為你做什麼？

column1: You can keep it, Sergeant. The U.S. Army's got it all in its data banks.
column2: 你可以拿著，警佐。美國軍隊的數據庫裡什麼都有。

column1: You take the printout of Michael Bain's military record.
column2: 你拿起了 Michael Bain 軍事檔案的列印件。

column1: Browsing through Michael Bains' military record, you come across the following information.
column2: 翻看 Michael Bains 的軍事檔案時，你找到了以下資訊。

column1: Career Gunnery Sergeant. Exemplary record, bearing and behavior - beyond reproach. Behavior alteration noticed following brother's death (Jesse Bains) at the hands of the police. Admitted to military psychiatric facility following a particulary violent outburst. Two injured.
column2: 職業砲手軍士。傑出的記錄、舉止和行為——無可挑剔。在哥哥（Jesse Bains）被警察殺害後表現出異常行為。因為一次特別暴力的爆發被送入軍隊精神病院。兩人受傷。

column1: Returned to active duty, but began displaying more violent, antisocial behavior patterns. Unprovoked physical attacks reported. Medical discharge from army for psychological instability.
column2: 返回現役，但開始表現出更多暴力的、反社會的行為模式。有過無故毆打他人的報告。因心理不穩定被軍隊醫療除役。

column1: The recruiter would no doubt flatten your face if you tried to walk out with his printer.
column2: 如果你試圖帶著他的列表機走出去，這個徵兵官毫無疑問會揍你。

column1: I don't think that's a good idea.
column2: 我認為那不是個好主意。
